selection.rule: Reuse Step 1 ascending Performance- ranking; exact numeric ties select the earliest CSV data row (1-based). No tolerance or setting preference.

historical_distribution.cdf_definition: Fraction of historical rows with Performance- <= recommended observation.

historical_reference.rule: Median Performance- of every historical measurement row, including duplicates; average the two middle values for an even count. This is a distribution reference, not an encoder configuration.
historical_reference.percent_rule: 100*(reference-recommended)/reference only for positive reference; otherwise null.

method.name: Marginal categorical eta squared
method.ranking: Variable settings by descending eta squared; exact ties share competition rank; alphabetical display tie break.
method.weighting: Every observed row equally weighted; exact numeric values form categories.
method.direction: Value-level mean minus overall mean and highest/lowest group means; independent of score.
method.inference: Exploratory; no significance tests, p-values or confidence intervals.
method.relationships: All variable pairs: Pearson correlation and exact equivalence of observed value partitions; neither implies causality.

diagnosis.client_explanation: Larger Performance- means worse measured encoding performance. The ranking prioritizes settings whose observed value groups separate overall mean outcomes most strongly. Use group means and counts to identify the values accompanying slower encodes. Correlated encoded choices can share credit; validate changes with controlled measurements.
limitations: Exploratory observational associations, not proven causal effects or significance tests; no p-values or multiplicity-adjusted claims.
Each setting is assessed marginally. Other settings, interactions, sampling imbalance and unrecorded workload or hardware can confound the ranking.
Correlated or redundant encodings can share the same association; their scores must not be added or interpreted as independent contributions.
Different indicators for one encoded choice can be mutually exclusive; changing one alone may be invalid. Names do not establish encoder semantics.
Eta squared measures separation of observed value-group means, not direction, fitted-model feature importance, or a guaranteed improvement.
All exact observed numeric values are treated as categories. Many levels and singleton groups can inflate eta squared; no out-of-sample guarantee is made.
Every row has equal weight, including duplicates. Counts are not independent replicate counts or uncertainty estimates.
Constants cannot support comparisons; zero score does not exclude interactions or distribution differences beyond the mean.
Performance- is minimized; physical units and output quality are unspecified. Larger means indicate worse measured outcomes, not a known number of seconds.
No model is fitted by this diagnosis, so model evaluation and random seed are not applicable. Step 2 prediction remains a separate holdout-evaluated tool.
Scores use floating-point arithmetic; exact score ties share competition rank and are displayed alphabetically. Near ties have no stability guarantee.
This is a retrospective recommendation among recorded rows, not an optimum over unseen configurations.
Selecting the minimum from the same history creates selection optimism; a single best observation supplies no statistical certainty or repeatability guarantee.
Historical rows may differ in workload, hardware, other settings, or unrecorded conditions. Rows are equally weighted, including duplicates; counts do not establish independent replication.
Setting-level group means and eta squared are marginal associations, not explanations of this individual outcome or causal effects. Correlated scores are never added.
Encoded setting names and values are preserved without inferring flag semantics or validity of unobserved combinations.
Performance- is minimized; physical units are unspecified. No output-quality, memory, or resource-use measurements are inferred.
No model predictions, p-values, confidence intervals, or significance claims are used in this justification. The historical median is not a randomized control.
Validate the candidate under the administrator's workload with repeated controlled measurements and required quality/resource checks before operational adoption.
Exact floating-point equality defines ties; near ties and rounding can affect ordering. Unsupported nonfinite computed statistics are rejected.
